shared_prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. One clear real-world documentary photograph for a Spanish-speaking beginner's English review. Natural everyday photographic detail, real material grain and plausible lighting, realistic anatomy and hands. NOT an illustration, collage, cutout, split panel or app UI. Full-bleed 3:2 landscape; no frames, internal padding, fake blur bands, watermarks, captions, speech bubbles, logos or readable words except an explicitly requested numeral. A first-time learner must recognize the meaning at phone size: the key person, action and object are large, sharp and inside the central safe area. Fresh scenes for this review only; never imitate a previous course photo. Ordinary anonymous people, never the recurring course cast (no Ana, Luis, Sofia or Diego).

One round analog wall clock with a plain white face and black hands hanging on a warm painted living-room wall, photographed straight on and centred. The clock shows exactly seven o'clock: the short hour hand points precisely at 7 and the long minute hand points precisely straight up at 12, with no second hand ambiguity. The clock face fills at least 45% of the frame height, is perfectly sharp and the numerals 1 to 12 are printed clearly. Nothing overlaps the clock face. No other clock, no people, no furniture in front of it, no readable words other than the clock numerals.

Use case: text-exact. A woman in her twenties standing at a kitchen wall calendar and pointing with her index finger at one day column, photographed from her side so both her face and the calendar are clear. The calendar is a simple weekly planner whose seven day columns are headed in English with clean printed capitals: MONDAY TUESDAY WEDNESDAY THURSDAY FRIDAY SATURDAY SUNDAY, spelled exactly like that and perfectly legible. Her fingertip touches the MONDAY column, which is circled in red marker. The calendar fills at least 45% of the frame width. Only those seven day names appear as text: no month name, no numbers, no notes, no other writing anywhere.
